name: Mechanical hot-metal linecasting
summary: A keyboard machine that assembled brass letter moulds and cast each whole line of text as one metal bar, making newspaper typesetting far faster than setting type by hand.
description: Keyboard-operated machine that assembles reusable letter matrices, justifies them, casts each line as a single metal slug, and redistributes the matrices.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.
why: Daily newspapers needed to set large amounts of text quickly, and hand composition was slow and labour-hungry.

market.note: The machine was used in a commercial newspaper production setting; earliest offer and first sale remain separate unknowns.

date.label: 2 July 1978
